A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, sampling pipeline and retained experiments. All 19 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original manually evaluated ProofNet experiments, filtering and selection ablations, sampling analyses and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original autoformalization experiments, benchmark corrections, metric-validation results and evaluations on research-level projects and additional benchmarks.

M1.justification: The sampling, filtering and selection backbone is retained. However, v2 introduces the BEqL and BEq+ symbolic evaluation procedures, including multi-strategy proof search in Algorithm 1, and implements a Lean symbolic-equivalence selector using BEq+ to cluster candidates (A.4.3). These are substantive computational additions.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from undergraduate ProofNet statements to research-project formalization with file context on RLM25, correctness classification on ProofNetVerif, competition mathematics on MiniF2F, and PDA's Basic, Random and Real scenarios. ProofNet# retains ProofNet's underlying informal statements while correcting their reference formalizations.

E2.justification: v2 adds symbolic-equivalence selection to the comparison in Figure 3, BEqL as a comparator for BEq+, and Lean Workbook-finetuned Llemma-7B to the retained ProofNet comparisons in Tables 8–9. The earlier greedy, random, majority-voting, Self-BLEU and attributed Codex comparators remain. The original LLM-backed BEq is discussed but is not directly evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds BEqL/BEq+ evaluation, pass@n measurements, temperature sweeps, sampling through n=1,000, and file-context controls. PDA evaluation samples 50 problems from each split. For retained ProofNet experiments, v1 counts prompt-leaked statements as incorrect, whereas v2 removes them (A.15). TEP reporting is dropped, and corrected references support the new reference-based metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds temperature sensitivity, extended sampling and selector comparisons, RLM25 context ablations, and metric-error analyses stratified by statement length. The filtering and n≤50 analyses persist with revisions. v1's analyses of human accuracy by statement length and accuracy conditional on successful type-checking are removed; the low-correction-effort study is retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds Kendall rank-correlation estimation alongside Pearson when validating metrics against 65 model/strategy results (Table 3). v1 reports Pearson correlations for type-checking versus accuracy. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many retained scores are revised: GPT-4o's greedy and Filter + Self-BLEU test accuracies change from 34.9% and 53.2% in v1 to 31.0% and 45.1% in v2. Changed exclusion handling prevents interpreting these as clean same-setting performance losses, and not every revision is explained. v2 also adds extensive benchmark and metric results; the low-correction-effort accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds proof-based criteria defining BEqL/BEq+ and an explicit counterexample where BEq+ accepts semantically mismatched divisibility statements (A.5). v1's brief argument about deduplication degenerating majority voting is omitted. Neither version develops a general theorem or proof analysis of the sampling method.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes a new three-step method and GPT-4o's 53.2% ProofNet accuracy. v2 broadens the main contributions to large-scale sampling, research-project evaluation, three benchmark resources and a CPU-only metric correlated with human evaluation. Its headline performance claim becomes gains of up to 18.4 percentage points.

C2.justification: v2 explains how low metric recall underestimates accuracy and documents a simplification-induced false positive. It identifies missing file context and candidate selection as practical bottlenecks, interprets retained theorems as implicit examples, and adds Lean Workbook contamination caveats. v1's discussion of reduced precision among type-checking candidates and untested deduplication is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds code/data access links, pinned research-project revisions and Lean versions, benchmark curation procedures, BEq+ tactic details, and a concrete RTX4090 inference timing. It newly documents checking each prediction twice. However, v1's Axolotl version, LoRA disclosure, checkpoint/epoch choices and fine-tuning hardware/time details disappear, reducing reproducibility for the retained fine-tuning experiments.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around prior type-check filtering, concurrent symbolic-equivalence selection, automated evaluation and contextual formalization. Section 2 newly discusses Agrawal et al., Li et al.'s semantic-consistency method, RAutoformalizer/BEq and related evaluation work. The contribution is consequently situated around scaling, metrics and benchmarks as well as the sampling pipeline.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized: Background becomes Related Work, metrics and benchmarks precede the sampling method, and detailed method descriptions and several earlier main-text analyses move into appendices. The abstract, contribution list, experimental narrative and discussion are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, adds an algorithm display and new experimental plots/tables, and expands existing tables with metric columns. v1 Figure 2 becomes separate appendix Figures 7–8; the filtering-ablation figure loses its type-check panel. Other figures are removed, and appendix examples gain framed displays. The original pipeline diagram is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly identifies manual-only evaluation and untested real-world applicability as limitations. v2 substantially addresses these through validated automated metrics, correction of 118 ProofNet references, and context-controlled evaluation on 619 research-project statements. These changes strengthen the evaluation foundation and practical relevance. Lost fine-tuning details and A.5's speculative comparison with original BEq on different samples are drawbacks, but the supported methodological and empirical gains provide a substantial net improvement.
